samples.summary: The self-healing upsert deletes/overwrites ANY trusted-author comment containing the marker, so a maintainer's or bot's quote-reply of the dashboard is destroyed
samples.evidence: `isOwnStatusComment` (loop-status.mjs:126-131) returns true for any comment whose body merely *contains* `<!-- agent-loop-status -->` when the author is a bot in `PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS` **or** any `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` human. The upsert then PATCHes `fresh[0]` (oldest) and, at loop-status.mjs:447-454, issues `DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{id}` for every younger match. GitHub's "Quote reply" copies the quoted comment's RAW markdown, HTML comments included, so a maintainer who quote-replies to the dashboard (or the agent quoting it in a self-review/report comment, posted as `yorkie-agent[bot]`, which is in the allow-list) produces a comment that satisfies this predicate with a HIGHER id than the real sticky comment — and the next update silently deletes it. The trust predicate was borrowed from `rounds.mjs::isPagedLatchComment`, where 'trusted human' is the right rule for *reading* a latch, but here it authorises a destructive write against comments this script did not author. A fix belongs on the new code: identify our own comment by author == the posting identity AND a marker at the start of the body (the render already puts it on line 1), and never delete a comment whose body is not marker-first.

samples.summary: set-state.mjs's reconcile still treats a bare `<!-- agent-paged -->` substring from ANY author as the CI paged latch, bypassing the author check this change establishes for that same marker in two new places
samples.evidence: This change hardens the CI arm's latch to an author-checked predicate (.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:163-176) and defines the same rule for the CI marker in `loop-status.mjs` (`CI_PAGED_LATCH` + `isAnyPagedLatchComment`, loop-status.mjs:73/104-108, with the public-repo reasoning spelled out in the header). The third consumer of the identical marker was not updated: `scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:238` does `comments.some((c) => (c.body || "").includes("<!-- agent-paged -->"))`, and `deriveState` treats that latch as dominant, so any GitHub account can still drive an agent PR's single-value state label to `agent:blocked` by pasting the marker (line 239 has the same gap for `<!-- agent-review-paged -->`). Impact is bounded to the label projection rather than the loop itself, but it now diverges from the rule two of its three siblings enforce.

samples.summary: Non-panel call sites omit --required-checks/--max-rounds, so the sticky comment's "Fix rounds used" flips between two different numbers as the arms take turns re-deriving the whole body
samples.evidence: `loop-status.mjs` counts rounds with `countCheckNames.length ? countCheckNames : lensCheckNames` (loop-status.mjs:~395) — i.e. the panel arm (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1009/1285/1449) passes the guard's `required_checks` and `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS`, while agent-iterate-ci.yml:235 and :440, agent-fix.yml:536 and agent-rerun.yml:234 pass neither. Because every update re-renders the body in full, the same PR's dashboard alternates between the guard-consistent "N of 3" and a manifest-wide count with no cap (the manifest is a superset of `required_checks` — inapplicable/non-blocking lenses are dropped from the latter, per review-panel.mjs:480-483), i.e. the CI-arm update can display a strictly larger budget figure than the number the round guard will actually page on. Passing `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS`/required checks (or having the script resolve them) from the other arms would make the projection stable.

samples.summary: The CI guard's new latch trust rule is a third literal copy of PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS/TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS with no test pinning it to rounds.mjs, unlike the marker literals which are pinned
samples.evidence: The repo's stated discipline for un-importable workflow copies is a pin test: `rounds.mjs:34-40` documents that `rounds.test.mjs` asserts the workflow's `PAGED_LATCH` copy is byte-identical, and the new `loop-status.test.mjs` pins `CI_PAGED_LATCH` against agent-iterate-ci.yml for exactly that reason. The new inline guard (.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:172-173) duplicates `PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS` and `TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS` from rounds.mjs:51/54 with no such pin, and this copy is a GUARD, not a projection: if rounds.mjs later adds or renames a paging identity (the comment there records the bot identity behind fixer pushes has already changed once), the CI arm silently stops recognising its own page comment and the CI-fix loop re-fires on a PR that was already handed to a human. A `wf.includes(...)`-style assertion over the two literals, next to the CI_PAGED_LATCH pin, closes it.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `isOwnStatusComment` (scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:114-118) matches ANY comment whose body merely contains `<!-- agent-loop-status -->` when `isTrustedAuthor` (loop-status.mjs:84-89) passes — allow-listed bots (`github-actions[bot]`, `yorkie-agent[bot]`, per .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:169) or any OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR human. There is no marker-first check and no comparison against the posting identity. The upsert (loop-status.mjs:436-455) then PATCHes `fresh[0]` (overwriting whatever that comment contained) and DELETEs every younger match, over the full issue-comment list returned by `listAllComments` (scripts/agent/metrics.mjs:859-862). Concrete, non-hypothetical collateral sites exist outside the diff: review-round-guard.mjs:90 posts the paged latch as a `github-actions[bot]` comment whose body embeds guard/finding prose (the latch that review-round-guard.mjs:117 and the panel gate read to stop the loop), and agent-review-on-demand.yml:554-596 publishes a bot comment assembled from lens `summary.md` files — `.agent-review/security/summary.md:3` in this tree already contains the literal marker, proving such trusted-author marker-bearing comments really occur. The writer is reachable from agent-review-panel.yml:1014/1284/1447/1764/1996, agent-fix.yml:536, agent-iterate-ci.yml:235/440 and agent-rerun.yml:234. In-lane for blast radius: the damaged sites are comments other modules author and depend on persisting, none of which appear in the diff.
